title: Steve Jobs on Apple's focus, hiring, and fixing what isn't great (Fortune, 2008)
summary: In this 2008 Fortune interview Jobs explains how Apple builds products it wants itself, says no to good ideas, and hires people who fall in love with the company. He also describes pushing the reset button on the iPhone design and running Apple through a top-100 team with weekly reviews.

principles.text: Focus means saying no to the hundred other good ideas, not just yes to one.
principles.quote: People think focus means saying yes to the thing you've got to focus on. But that's not what it means at all. It means saying no to the hundred other good ideas that there are. You have to pick carefully.

principles.text: Build what you yourself want; don't rely on market research or consultants.
principles.quote: It's not about pop culture, and it's not about fooling people, and it's not about convincing people that they want something they don't. We figure out what we want.

principles.text: When hiring senior people, competence is the minimum; what matters is whether they fall in love with the company.
principles.quote: competence is the ante. They have to be really smart. But the real issue for me is, Are they going to fall in love with Apple? Because if they fall in love with Apple, everything else will take care of itself.

principles.text: Be willing to throw away a year of work when you don't love the product.
principles.quote: I just don't love this. I can't convince myself to fall in love with this. And this is the most important product we've ever done." "And we pushed the reset button.

principles.text: Take responsibility for the complete user experience; control hardware and software together.
principles.quote: we think that our job is to take responsibility for the complete user experience. And if it's not up to par, it's our fault, plain and simply.

principles.text: A leader's job is to push great people to be better, and to keep them informed so they can decide as well as you.
principles.quote: My job is to not be easy on people. My job is to make them better.
